newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer Dome offers $5 billion merger to Bre-X.
newsitem.headline: Placer Dome offers $5 billion merger to Bre-X.

text.p: Canadian miner Placer Dome Inc. offered to merge on Tuesday with Bre-X Minerals Ltd. in a deal that seeks to thwart Barrick Gold Corp.'s bid for Bre-X's rich Busang gold discovery in Indonesia.

The Indonesian government late last year told Bre-X to form a joint venture with Barrick on Busang in northern Borneo and the two companies have worked on a deal for months. But delays have prompted analysts to speculate that the Indonesian government might now be prepared to allow another bidder.
In a letter to Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh on Monday, Placer offered a stock-for-stock "merger of equals" at a "significant" premium to Bre-X's current share price.

Placer unveiled its offer after recently receiving encouragement from unidentified sources in Indonesia. "We have the sense that there is indeed a green light," said Placer's Chief Executive John Willson.
Placer did not announce the precise terms of its offer but Willson said Bre-X shareholders would end up with 45 to 55 percent of the combined company.
He pegged the deal's value at C$6.75 billion ($5 billion), or roughly half the value of the combined companies.

Placer also offered up to 40 percent of the project to Indonesian interests including the government and said it would build a C$2.3 billion ($1.7 billion) mine at Busang. Gold production would start in 1999 and average about 3 million to 4 million ounces a year.

Busang is believed to be one of the richest gold finds in history and a number of companies in Indonesia and Canada have been involved in complex behind-the-scenes machinations to try and grab part of its riches.
The deposit is known to contain 57 million ounces of gold, and analysts believe it may hold up to 100 million ounces.

News of the Placer offer sent Bre-X shares soaring C$1.90 ($1.41) to C$23.35 ($17.30) in Toronto. Placer Dome's stock lost C90 cents (67 cents) to C$28.10 ($20.81) while Barrick stock dropped C95 cents (70 cents) to C$35.45 ($26.26).

Bre-X welcomed the offer, but said it would have to study it before responding. Bre-X Chief Executive Walsh said in an interview he believed Placer had a good chance of opening up the bidding process.
"Placer Dome has cast a whole new light on this project," he said in a telephone interview.
But Barrick spokesman Vince Borg said in Toronto that there was no room for Placer in the negotiations for Busang.

Analysts reckoned the value of Placer's offer would likely work out to be between C$26 ($19.26) and C$35 ($25.93) a share for Bre-X, depending on how the pooling of shares was split. If Bre-X and Placer entered a 50-50 deal, the offer would be worth about the same as Placer's current share price.
Exact terms for Calgary-based Bre-X's joint venture with Barrick have not been disclosed, but analysts estimated its value at C$25 ($18.52) to C$28 ($20.74) a share.
That deal called for Barrick to own 67.5 percent of the discovery, with Bre-X getting 22.5 percent and the Indonesian government 10 percent.

While Placer has expressed interest for months in bidding for Busang, its offer was well-timed, analysts said. "They stand a very good chance," said gold analyst Michael Fowler with brokerage Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion.
The Indonesian government has clearly favoured a deal with Barrick in the past, but there were hints officials may be open to an auction for Bre-X, he said.

While it had no word from the Indonesian government, Placer held out high hopes for success. "We believe there will be a positive response," said Willson, adding that the process could take weeks or months to unwind.

He said there was growing dismay in Indonesia over criticism that it was unfair to force Bre-X into a deal with Barrick and also a sense that the Indonesian government should get a bigger stake than the 10 percent contained in the Barrick deal.
Placer said it would not be surprised to find itself in a bidding war over Bre-X with at least four other companies including Barrick if Jakarta opened up the bidding process.
